# Wayne Smith Trucking celebrates 50 years in business

Mon, October 12, 2026 by Rich Moellers

Wayne Smith Trucking of Morrilton celebrated 50 years in business Friday with a special open house event. Representatives from the local business community joined the company’s business partners and elected officials to mark five decades of growth for the company. The late Wayne Smith founded the company in 1976 with two used trucks and five trailers. Today, it operates 115 trucks, 600 trailers, and employs about 170 people, serving customers across the lower 48 states.

President Neil Corder, Smith’s son-in-law, joined the company in 1993, when it had about 30 trucks. He says the company’s success comes down to time, good people, and the right opportunities – including the early days, when Green Bay Packaging helped them get started.

# County celebrates Strimbus’ centennial

Posted by Joe Pinchot | Sep 30, 2026 | America 250, Business | 0 | 

Trumbull County commissioners on Aug. 19 adopted a resolution acknowledging and congratulating the Strimbu family and Nick Strimbu Inc. of Brookfield for the company reaching 100 years of service to the community.

The meeting was attended by Bill Strimbu, the recently retired president, and his sons Spencer and Harrison, who have taken over company leadership and are the fourth generation of Strimbus to run the trucking and logistics company.

Bill Strimbu thanked the commissioners, their predecessors, the various trustees of Brookfield and Hubbard townships and the various police and fire chiefs who have served over the years for “ nothing but cooperation.”

“It really helps when you’re running a business and you have cooperation,” he said. “We appreciate it.”

The commissioners noted how the company’s existence has benefited the county in terms of the service it has provided, its commitment to safety, the jobs it has provided and its philanthropic efforts, such as the Strimbu Memorial Foundation.

# Wagner Logistics to Add Nearly 80 Jobs with New High-Volume Logistics Operation in Liberty

 Wagner Logistics 

Oct 14, 2026, 08:54 ET

NORTH KANSAS CITY, Mo., Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Wagner Logistics, a nationwide provider of third-party logistics, today announced it has signed a multi-year agreement with a Kansas City-area manufacturer to launch a new manufacturing support and warehouse operations program in Liberty, Mo.

The new operation includes two leased warehouse facilities in the Liberty area totaling more than 830,000 square feet. Wagner expects to add 79 new local jobs over the next two years, starting immediately. The company will also make a multi-million-dollar investment in equipment, infrastructure and automated trailer loading and unloading technology to support the operation.

"This is exactly the kind of operation where Wagner's strengths come through," said Brian Smith, President and Chief Executive Officer of Wagner Logistics. "It requires speed, flexibility, close coordination and the ability to design a solution around what the customer actually needs."

Hollingsworth Logistics is adding 150 jobs and consolidating its operations near San Antonio with a new 340,000-square-foot warehouse at Park35. The expansion will retain 224 current employees and supports growing regional warehousing demand.

By

Workers and visitors gather inside an industrial facility as Hollingsworth Logistics Group expands near San Antonio.

A Michigan-based logistics company is expanding its operations near San Antonio, Texas, with plans to add 150 jobs and consolidate two existing facilities into a 340,090-square-foot warehouse along Interstate 35.

Hollingsworth Logistics Group has signed a seven-year lease at Park35, a growing industrial development in Schertz, northeast of San Antonio. The expansion will retain 224 existing positions, bringing the company's planned local workforce to 374 employees.
